Fixes #6536.

## What went wrong

Every conversion and move mutation is gated on an in-memory policy built in the `ConversionResolverMutations` constructor. Its role list is the entire check — the policy is in-memory, so no credential rule in the database can widen it.

`67bc7945f` ("initial pass at updating global roles", May 2024) renamed the global role `global-admin-spaces` to `global-support`. Throughout that commit the symbol was renamed in place and kept in its lists:

```diff
-  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
+  AuthorizationCredential.GLOBAL_SUPPORT,
```

At this one call site it was deleted instead of renamed:

```diff
-    [
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN,
-      AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN_SPACES,
-    ],
+    [AuthorizationRoleGlobal.GLOBAL_ADMIN],
```

Holders of the role now called `global-support` silently lost access to all seven mutations sharing this policy: `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `convertSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL0`, `moveSpaceL1ToSpaceL2`, `moveSpaceL2ToSpaceL1`, `convertVirtualContributorToUseKnowledgeBase`.

It reads as a rename that missed a call site rather than a deliberate restriction — nothing in that commit suggests an intent to narrow conversions. **If the narrowing was intentional, this PR should be closed and #6536 answered instead**; I could not find anything recording that intent.

## What this changes

Restores `GLOBAL_SUPPORT` to the role list, and adds a test asserting the list. Nothing covered it before, which is exactly why the rename went unnoticed — the existing specs mock `grantAccessOrFail`, so they pass whatever the roles are.

This also realigns the gate with `createPlatformCredentialRules`, which grants `PLATFORM_ADMIN` to `global-admin`, `global-support` and `global-license-manager`. Before this change a caller could hold `PLATFORM_ADMIN` on the platform and still be refused here.

## Verification

- `vitest run conversion.resolver.mutations.spec.ts` — 20 passed.
- Negative control: reverting the one-line source change fails the new test with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ [ 'global-admin', …(1) ], …(2) ]`, so it does guard the regression.
- `biome check` clean on both files.

## Deliberately left out

Two things surfaced in #6536 that made this hard to diagnose but are separate changes:

- `global-license-manager` also holds `PLATFORM_ADMIN` platform-side but is not in this list. I have not added it — widening beyond restoring the lost role is a product call, not a regression fix.
- The failure logs `on authorization undefined of type 'in-memory'`, which reads like a missing policy and sends you looking in the database. The policy name is already passed to the constructor and would point straight at the real check.

Adds a nullable `CollaboraDocument.previewUrl` field so clients can render a
thumbnail of a saved Collabora document without opening the editor.
`workspace#059-collabora-preview-streaming`.

## What this does

`previewUrl` resolves the existing internal backing `Document` relation and
returns the same-origin authorized path built from its stable `fileID`:

```
/api/private/wopi/files/{fileID}/preview
```

It returns `null` when no backing file exists, which is why the field is
nullable — a legacy or orphaned `CollaboraDocument` can lack the relation.

Deliberate properties:

- **The backing `Document` is never exposed** through GraphQL, and no WOPI
  editor token is issued. Only the stable `fileID` crosses the boundary, per
  ADR `0012`.
- **The URL is not a bearer credential.** Normal `CollaboraDocument` field
  authorization applies here, and the WOPI endpoint independently re-authorizes
  every byte request against the source document's current policy.
- **`/wopi-private/...` is an internal router path** — never returned to
  GraphQL, never constructed by the client. The gateway rewrites the public
  path onto it.
- The `fileID` is URL-encoded.

## Schema impact

Additive only: one nullable field, **zero breaking changes** per `schema:diff`.
Existing `CollaboraDocument` field authorization is unchanged.

## Tests

Resolver and service unit tests cover a present backing file, a missing relation
resolving to `null`, stable-`fileID` URL encoding, and that existing field
authorization still gates the field. Verified live against a booted stack via
GraphQL probes, including an introspection check that the field is a nullable
`String` and that no `Document`-typed field was added to `CollaboraDocument`.

## Known follow-up

`previewUrl` performs a per-document `findOne` with the `document` relation, and
there is no `CollaboraDocument` dataloader in `src/core/dataloader`, so a
callouts list selecting the field issues one backing-document query per item.
Raised in review and tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed here: the loader
belongs alongside the existing dataloader creators and should batch the
`document` relation for the list path generally, not only for `previewUrl`.
It is a performance regression on an existing list surface, not a correctness
defect — flagging for the maintainers' call on whether it blocks merge.

## Ordering

This field can deploy before anything consumes it, but it must not be relied on
until the WOPI endpoint and its gateway route are reachable in the target
environment. See the rollout ordering in the workspace spec's `plan.md`.

## Spec

`agents-hq/specs/059-collabora-preview-streaming/` —
`contracts/graphql-preview-url.md`, `tasks/server.md`.

Closes #6021

Related (remain open until manually closed): alkem-io/server#4970, alkem-io/client-web#9353.

Workspace spec: `workspace#063-callout-transfer-flow-state` — https://github.com/alkem-io/agents-hq/tree/feat/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/specs/063-callout-transfer-flow-state/

## What was still broken after #6339

QA re-tested #6021 after #6339 merged and acceptance criterion 3 ("same logic applies when the destination's innovation flow was changed via template", the alkem-io/client-web#9353 sequence) still failed: the transferred callout is tagged with one of the destination's **old** state names and shows on no flow tab.

## Root cause (proven at code level)

The transfer logic from #6339 is correct but validates against the destination's flow-state `TagsetTemplate` (`allowedValues` / `defaultSelectedValue`), and that template drifts from the `InnovationFlow`'s actual states through three writers:

1. **Template apply** — `updateCollaborationFromSpaceTemplate` loads the target collaboration with `calloutsSet.tagsetTemplateSet` (eager `tagsetTemplates`, `cascade: true` on every hop). `updateInnovationFlowStates` updates a *separately loaded* copy of the template and saves it; the applier's final `collaborationService.save(targetCollaboration)` then cascades the **stale** in-memory template back over the row, reverting `allowedValues`/`defaultSelectedValue` to the pre-template names. The destination's own callouts stay visible (they are re-homed by state *name*), which is why only transfers exposed it.
2. **Add / delete a single state** — neither `createStateOnInnovationFlow` nor `deleteStateOnInnovationFlow` ever rewrote the template.
3. **Rename** — `TagsetService.updateTagsetsSelectedValue` re-tagged callouts in memory on the rename branch and `continue`d without `save`; nothing cascades to those tagsets, so callouts in a renamed phase kept the old name on reload.

## Fix (behaviour-only; no DDL, no GraphQL change)

- `TemplateApplierService`: re-read the callouts set's `TagsetTemplateSet` after the flow-state update, so the cascade save persists the current vocabulary and template-added callouts are classified against it.
- `InnovationFlowService`: add/delete state rewrite the flow-state template; one shared default rule (`resolveDefaultFlowStateName`: current state while it exists, else first) now backs template apply, rename, add and delete.
- `TagsetService`: persist the re-tag on the rename branch.
- Migration `1789000000000-ResyncFlowStateTagsetTemplates` (data-only, idempotent, no-op `down`): re-derives `allowedValues` from the flow's states in flow order, repairs a missing/unknown default, and moves callout flow-state tags that match no state (case-insensitively) to that default. Existing drifted spaces (acceptance, where QA reproduced this) are healed on deploy.

Memo signing renders the live Yjs projection and resolves every internal image through document metadata and file-service bytes. Existing memos can still reference a document whose metadata row is absent, or whose metadata exists while the backing bytes return a typed 404. ## What / why

A persona on the **generic** engine had no server-side route to receive a stored prompt graph: the invocation builder attached `promptGraph` only inside the `EXPERT` branch. So the declarative graph support merged in [virtual-contributor#122](https://github.com/alkem-io/virtual-contributor/pull/122) (conditional edges, retrieve/echo nodes, the shipped workshop payload) was live but **unreachable through configuration**.

This adds a `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES` allowlist covering `expert` + `generic-openai`, new GraphQL authoring fields for the node/edge forms, an activation guide, and the workshop authoring fixture.

Closes #6385. Spec: `workspace#053-generic-prompt-graph`.

## What actually changed in production code

Most of the diff is tests and docs, but **three source files change existing behaviour** — worth reading rather than skimming:

**`ai.persona.resolver.mutations.ts` — the `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` body was restructured, not extended.** The fetch and the authorization check moved inside a `try`, an audit call was added on both the success and failure paths, and a constructor dependency was added. **The authorization check is unchanged in substance and still runs before any update**: same `grantAccessOrFail`, same `AuthorizationPrivilege.UPDATE`, same policy object, same position relative to the mutation — only its enclosing block moved. That is the property to verify when reviewing this hunk, and it is why the restructure is called out here instead of being described as an addition.

**`ai.persona.service.ts` — two conditions changed.** `input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT` became `PROMPT_GRAPH_ENGINES.includes(input.engine)`; that is the feature. A second condition was *tightened*: `if (!invocationGraph)` became `if (!invocationGraph && input.engine === AiPersonaEngine.EXPERT)`, deliberately keeping the default-graph fallback expert-only so a generic persona with no stored graph produces **no `promptGraph` key at all** rather than inheriting expert's default.

**`prompt.graph.node.dto.ts` / `prompt.graph.edge.dto.ts` / `ai.persona.dto.update.ts`** add nullable fields; the only removal is an import line being widened.

Genuinely additive: every new test file, the docs, and the fixture. **No pre-existing test was modified or deleted** (`git diff origin/develop..HEAD -- '**/*.spec.ts' | grep -c '^-'` = 0), and the **GraphQL schema** delta is additive — 21 added, 0 breaking.

## Decisions worth reviewing

- **The story said "GENERIC"; there is no such enum value.** It is `AiPersonaEngine.GENERIC_OPENAI` (`generic-openai`) — the routing key bound to the `virtual-contributor-engine-generic` queue.
- **The allowlist deliberately excludes** `guidance`, `openai-assistant`, `libra-flow`, `community-manager`: widening requires engine-side graph execution first. A future enum value defaults to *not* attaching.
- **No validation of the graph/body-of-knowledge pairing.** `bodyOfKnowledgeID` is per-invocation from the VC, not stored on the persona, so the server cannot validate it. A retrieve-bearing graph on a BoK-less persona hard-fails at engine parse time and the member sees the standard error response — a documented precondition, not a defect.
- **No migration**: `ai_persona.promptGraph` jsonb already existed engine-independently.
- Expert behaviour is byte-identical in all three modes (stored / default / none).

## Evidence

- **8170 tests pass / 711 files**. Lint, typecheck, build clean.
- `AiPersonaInvocationInput` remains **absent** from `schema.graphql` (count 0).
- The authoring fixture parses through the **actual merged VC engine parser** (`2920c83`): 8 nodes, 2 conditional edges, state model built.

## Review round (8 findings, all fixed, 0 declined)

Two independent reviewers on different providers found non-overlapping defects:

**Security** (verdict was `conditional`, now remediated):
- `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` wrote **no audit record** — a global admin could change the graph governing prompts, retrieval and member output with no attributable trace. Now audits success *and* failure with actor / persona / engine / `promptGraphChanged` only; never the graph, prompt text or credentials (SOC 2 CC7.2·CC7.3, ISO A.8.15·A.8.16). **This is what motivated the resolver restructure described above.**
- The activation guide didn't disclose that retrieve nodes send body-of-knowledge content to the **external model provider**; it now requires a data-classification check before activation.
- `edge.map` was an unbounded JSON scalar → now bounded (string→string, 100 entries, 128 chars per key/value). Structural limits only; graph semantics stay the engine's job.

**Correctness** — two of these were caught by *mutating the production code and watching the tests stay green*:
- The **round-trip test was tautological**: the mocked repository assigns by reference, so it compared an object to itself. Gutting the transformer left it passing. It now crosses the transformer/JSON seam against a separately constructed object.
- The **matrix's expert-default row** asserted only `toBeDefined()` — replacing the default graph with `{nodes:[],edges:[]}` kept it 7/7 green. It now asserts real graph content.
- **`schema.graphql` had been hand-authored**, including a *fabricated* description for the JSON scalar and wrong field ordering (~80 lines of divergence from the generator). Regenerated with the repo's own tooling and committed verbatim; this also picks up a pre-existing description drift on `develop`.

Full evidence ledger: `specs/053-generic-prompt-graph/forge-run.md` in the workspace repo.

## Activation (after merge)

Store the payload on a generic persona via `aiServerUpdateAiPersona` — see `docs/prompt-graphs.md`, which covers the walkthrough, the body-of-knowledge precondition, the provider-egress check, and the per-top-level-key merge behaviour (send `promptGraph: null` first for a clean replace).

## Problem

Two failure modes in production (alkem-io/alkemio#2122) produce no user feedback or ugly raw error messages:

| Mode | Server response | What the user saw |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Redis session timeout** | 503 `{ error: "session_store_unavailable" }` | **Nothing** — completely silent |
| **B — pg-pool exhaustion** | GraphQL error, code `UNSPECIFIED` | Two ugly toasts: "An error occurred with code UNSPECIFIED" + "timeout exceeded when trying to connect" |
| **Offline / DNS / fetch failure** | No response | **Nothing** |

**Root cause:** `handleNetworkErrors` only checked for `result.errors` (plural, GraphQL envelope). The 503 body has `error` (singular, REST shape) — silent miss. `handleSendMessage` then swallowed whatever remained.

## Fix

**One shared notification path for GraphQL errors**, used by both the normal (HTTP 200) and network-embedded (non-200) handlers:

| Change | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Extract `notifyGraphQLError` | `useApolloErrorHandler.ts` | Single function translates + notifies a GraphQL error — eliminates the inconsistency where network-path errors were shown raw while normal-path errors were translated |
| Handle REST-style `{ error }` body | `useApolloErrorHandler.ts` | Maps known error codes (e.g. `session_store_unavailable`) to i18n keys; unknown codes get a generic fallback |
| Catch-all for network failures | `useApolloErrorHandler.ts` | Offline, DNS, timeout — anything with no parseable body gets "A connection problem occurred" |
| Suppress raw detail for `UNSPECIFIED` | `useApolloErrorHandler.ts` | Internal server messages (like pg-pool timeout text) are noise for users |
| Add `UNSPECIFIED` to enum | `errors.ts` | Was a bare string; now uses `AlkemioGraphqlErrorCode.UNSPECIFIED` like every other code comparison |
| Guard empty `errors` array | `useApolloErrorHandler.ts` | `Array.isArray()` + `.length > 0` — previously `errors[0]` on `[]` would crash |
| i18n keys × 6 languages | `common.{en,nl,es,bg,de,fr}.json` | `UNSPECIFIED`, `network.session_store_unavailable`, `network.generic` |

## Result

| Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| A: Redis session timeout | Silent | "The service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." |
| B: pg-pool / unspecified | Two ugly toasts | "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again." |
| Offline / DNS | Silent | "A connection problem occurred. Please check your connection and try again." |

## Context

Full root cause analysis with Kibana evidence, Redis SLOWLOG + INFO memory diagnostics, and infrastructure recommendations posted in alkem-io/alkemio#2122.

Closes alkem-io/alkemio#2122

## What

On phone-width screens the header breadcrumbs — previously hidden below `md` —
become a compact **location-hierarchy disclosure**: a `…` pill next to the home
logo opens a panel listing the full trail, Home first, each ancestor a tappable
link with its existing avatar, the current location tinted and badged.

Fixes alkem-io/client-web#9901

## Why

Issue #2109 asked for a "back" affordance in the native app. The scope was
refined to the real need: on phones there is no way to see where you are or
step back up the hierarchy. This reuses the **existing desktop breadcrumb data
and destinations** verbatim and restyles them for small screens.

**No functional navigation changes.** No new routes, no data or GraphQL change,
no new runtime dependency (`package.json` and the lockfile are untouched).

## How

- **Viewport width is the only trigger.** The wrapper is `md:hidden`, the exact
  complement of the desktop trail's `hidden md:inline-flex`, so exactly one
  presentation exists at any width. **No user-agent, webview or native-bridge
  detection anywhere** — the same behavior applies in the native shell, an
  embedded webview and a plain mobile browser.
- New CRD component `MobileBreadcrumbs.tsx` built on the existing Radix-backed
  dropdown primitive. `CrumbVisual` is extracted from `BreadcrumbsTrail.tsx` so
  both presentations render identity visuals identically — a render-identical
  refactor, locked by a DOM-parity test.
- Glue is a 10-line change in `CrdLayoutWrapper.tsx`; trail publishers untouched.
- Four new `crd-layout` keys, translated across all six locales.

### Header fit

Live verification found the disclosure's chevron **invisible** on a header
carrying the authenticated icon cluster — not clipped, but painted over by the
icon nav sliding across it. Measured at authenticated density:

| Width | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 360 | overlap −69px | **clear +27px** |
| 390 | overlap −39px | **clear +57px** |
| 430 | — | **clear +97px** |

Fixed by removing the separator glyph, shrinking the ellipsis box from the
primitive's 36px default to 20px (the trigger still meets the 44px touch
target), and reducing the header's side padding **below `md` only** — which also
closes dead space before the logo and after the avatar.

`Header.tsx` is therefore touched, deliberately and against the original plan:
the defect is in the header's own flex layout and cannot be fixed from the
component. **Every `md:` value is the pre-existing one**, so at ≥768px the
computed classes are byte-identical to `develop`. Note the blast radius is
wider than the trail: phone header spacing changes on every page, including
pages with no breadcrumbs.

Localized accessible name (not "…"), `aria-expanded`, `aria-current="page"` on
the current row — which stays **focusable** rather than Radix-`disabled`, so
screen readers still reach it. Full keyboard operation verified end to end:

and restores focus to the trigger. Touch target 44×44 at every width.

At **320px** with the authenticated icon cluster the nav still overlaps the

and the callout detail dialog, replacing the flat document-type placeholder with
the document's actual first page. `workspace#059-collabora-preview-streaming`.

## What this does

Consumes the new nullable `CollaboraDocument.previewUrl` (server#6511) and maps
it through to the CRD presentational layer:

- `previewUrl` added to the `CollaboraDocumentGate` fragment and the contribution
  selections, with codegen regenerated.
- `calloutDataMapper` / `contributionDataMapper` map it to card props; the
  connectors thread it into `CalloutCollaboraPreview` and
  `ContributionDocumentCard`.
- The type icon stays mounted and visible until the image actually loads, and
  returns on error — so a failed or unavailable render degrades to exactly the
  previous UI rather than an empty box.
- The image is decorative: `alt=""`, `loading="lazy"`, no second accessible name.
  The card keeps its existing document name and type, announced once.

Load state is tracked **by URL value rather than a boolean**, so a later
`previewUrl` change — a re-render producing a new preview file ID — starts in the
correct not-yet-loaded state without a reset effect.

## Verification

Live-verified against a booted stack from the feature worktrees, and persisted as
three durable `@forge-acceptance` Playwright suites:

- `e2e/specs/collaboraPreviewRendering.e2e.spec.ts` — the card and dialog render
  real content, lazy loading, decorative-image accessibility.
- `e2e/specs/collaboraPreviewAuthorization.e2e.spec.ts` — non-member `403`,
  revoked reader with a genuine ETag getting `403` not `304`, anonymous access,
  forged-header rejection, public-root isolation.
- `e2e/specs/collaboraPreviewCaching.e2e.spec.ts` — one render per saved state,
  cache hit across sessions, atomic re-swap after a save, single-flight.

Every scenario that asserts on rendered pixels skips when the renderer is
unavailable (`502`/`503`) rather than reporting a product failure — Collabora
being down is a designed-for state, and the card is asserted to fall back to type
artwork and stay interactive.

Unit coverage: 155 tests across the callout, contribution and data-mapper scopes.

### A note for whoever tunes the e2e fixture

The compact feed card is a short `h-28` box using `object-cover` with default
**centre** positioning, so a 1200×630 render of a page whose content sits at the
top is cropped to the blank middle and looks very close to the placeholder. Two
verification runs reported a false rendering defect because of this before it was
traced. `E2E_PREVIEW_FILE_ID`'s document must carry a distinct high-contrast fill
covering a large fraction of the page, so the pixel assertion is a real sensor
rather than a coin flip on crop geometry.

## Ordering

User-visible wave — merge last. This must not ship before the WOPI endpoint and
its gateway route are reachable in the target environment, or every card falls
back to the type icon. See the rollout ordering in the workspace spec's `plan.md`.

## What & why

Cross-service coverage for the contribution notify switch (`alkem-io/notifications#593`) — the API-level pins plus one persisted acceptance walk.

## What's here

**`post-contribution.it-spec.ts` — four appended cases** (`+162` lines, **zero deletions**; the six pre-existing cases are byte-identical):

| case | pins |
|---|---|
| `sendNotification: false` suppresses the member **and** the admin notification | the AC3-literal ruling (D-OP2), so it is deliberate behaviour and not drift |
| `sendNotification: true` notifies exactly as today | same recipients and content as the omitted-flag path |
| **omitting** `sendNotification` still notifies everyone | the wire default stays notify — the regression this feature could most plausibly cause |
| the activity log entry is written even though `sendNotification` is false | AC4 |

Plus a regenerated lib GraphQL client, a flag-aware `createPostOnCalloutWithNotification` helper (the legacy `createPostOnCallout` is left **untouched** so its ~68–104 call sites keep omitting the field), and a persisted Playwright walk `client-web/tests/contribution-notify-switch.spec.ts` covering US1-AS1…AS5.

**Extend-never-edit is mechanically verifiable**: the diff against the branch point is insertions only for the pre-existing specs.

Status: `post-contribution.it-spec.ts` runs **9/9 green** against a live stack (5 pre-existing + 4 new).

## Four defects this slice had, and what they teach

These were caught by live verification and adversarial review, and are worth reading as review notes rather than trivia — three of the four were tests that *looked* green while asserting nothing:

1. **Two collection-time dereferences.** The describe block read `baseScenario` (and later `TestUserManager.users`) at describe scope, before `beforeAll` populates them. The file threw during collection, so **zero** tests ran — taking the pre-existing cases down with it. A green suite summary elsewhere hid it.
2. **A vacuous pin.** The new describe is a *sibling* of `Notifications - post`, so it never inherited that block's `enablePostNotifications` — and the preceding test deliberately **disables** notifications for every role. The suppression case therefore passed even though it could not fail: with notifications off for everyone, "no mail arrived" proves nothing. Fixed by mirroring the enable list in the describe's own `beforeAll`.
3. **Shared-state leak.** An earlier fix re-enabled notifications for eight globally-seeded personas without restoring them, flipping the state handed to the rest of the serial run and breaking an untouched neighbouring spec. Not visible in a single-file re-run.
4. **Ungated queue assertions.** The acceptance walk asserted through the RabbitMQ management API without the repo's `rabbitMqManagementConfigured()` guard, while the nightly workflow sets no `RABBITMQ_MANAGEMENT_*` — so its emission checks would have gone green when the queue simply did not exist.

Related, worth knowing when running the notification suites locally: these specs share one MailSlurper mailbox and clobber each other's counts when run in parallel — `community-updates.it-spec.ts` passes 5/5 alone but fails in the directory sweep. Run spec **files** one at a time.

## Security note — please read

The persisted walk signs in through the Kratos **UI**, so `AUTH_TEST_HARNESS_PASSWORD` is typed into the page. The nightly config sets `retries: 2` with `trace: 'on-all-retries'` and `video: 'retain-on-failure'`, and `scripts/publish-report.sh` pushes report attachments — **`data/**` included** — to the `gh-pages` branch of this **public** repo. Any flake would therefore publish that plaintext credential to the public site.

This PR adds `use: { trace: 'off', video: 'off' }` to the new nightly project, so **this walk cannot contribute a copy**.

**It does not fix the underlying channel.** The publishing path predates this feature and, per the security review, the exposure is already realised by an existing sibling walk. Three actions remain **open and are not addressed here**: rotating `AUTH_TEST_HARNESS_PASSWORD`, purging `playwright/**/data/**` from `gh-pages` history, and stripping attachments before publishing (or making the Pages site private). Raising these with the repo owners is recommended independently of this PR.

Runs the nightly `server-api` suite in parallel — **79.2 min → 44.5 min (~1.8×)**, measured on `test-alkem.io` — without weakening a single assertion. All 108 files still run; nothing is skipped,
  deleted or quarantined to gain speed.

  `workspace#040-parallel-nightly-server-api` · story #570

  ## How it works

  The 108-file `nightly` project becomes two projects in the **same** config, run as **one** invocation: `nightly-parallel` (94 files, `groupOrder: 0`, `maxWorkers` from `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS`) and
  `nightly-serial` (14 files, `groupOrder: 1`, `maxWorkers: 1`). Sequential groups give lane separation without a second config or a report merge. The legacy `nightly` project is left **byte-untouched**
  as the rollback surface — reverting is one line in `package.json`.

  Lane membership is **derived, never hand-maintained**: a guard applies hazard rules with name-scoped transitive taint, proves the two lanes partition the nightly scope exactly, and fails closed on
  drift. New spec files default to serial until proven safe — which is how two specs that arrived from `develop` mid-flight were classified with no manual step.

  Three mechanisms protect the signal: **serial-confirm** (any parallel failure is re-run at one worker, and the *serial* verdict is the job's exit code; parallel-fail/serial-pass is logged as
  interference and demotes a file after ≥2 in 7 nights), the **lane guard**, and a **retrospective baseline diff**.

  ## The main finding

  Four static-analysis passes added rules and demoted 22 files, and each run still found interference the rules missed. Two runs on identically fresh databases gave **7 and 63 failures** — same code, same
  data. Every one adjudicated as interference, never a real defect.

  The hazardous pattern is *"assert a shared pool user's privileged action succeeds"* — most of the suite, and not soundly detectable statically. The server compounds it: the `ActorContext` cache is keyed
  by actor alone and **deleted** on any credential change for that actor anywhere.

  So the sharing was removed. **Each vitest worker now gets its own 13 identities** (slot from `VITEST_POOL_ID`; worker 0 keeps bare addresses, worker N uses plus-addressing). Under `pool: 'threads'` a
  worker runs one file at a time, so two concurrently-executing files **cannot** resolve the same identity — structural, not heuristic. On `test-alkem.io` a full run then came back **`exit=0`, 108/108 
  files, 2003 passed, zero failures**.

  This needed a non-obvious fix: `GLOBAL_ADMIN` is granted by the server's bootstrap against the literal `admin@alkem.io`, so per-worker admins were unprivileged and every global-admin scenario failed
  `FORBIDDEN_POLICY`. The harness now grants platform roles per slot at startup using worker 0's bootstrap-privileged token.

  ## Teardown was silently broken

  `cleanUpBaseScenario` wrapped its whole delete sequence in **one** `try`, so the first failure skipped every delete after it. And `deleteOrganization` fails while the account still hosts anything — with
  the org **last**, that failure was invisible. An organisation leaked on essentially every run, of every suite using the factory.

  Measured: wall-clock rose **20.5 → 28.7 min across six consecutive runs**, then dropped straight back to 21.1 when the database was recreated. **~36% of runtime was accumulated residue** — larger than
  every optimisation here combined.

  Teardown is now per-entity best-effort and enumerates what the account still hosts, deleting in the required order (L2 → L1 → L0 → VCs → packs → org). Verified behaviourally: the organisation is
  genuinely gone afterwards, including when an untracked resource was created under its account.

  ## Also here

  - **`uploads.it-spec.ts` is green** — long red because an organisation profile's first visual is an AVATAR, aspect-ratio-locked to 1:1, and the fixture was 410×256. The server was right; the fixture was
  stale.
  - **Environment allowlist guard** — refuses to provision identities against an unapproved host. The Kratos *admin* path bypasses the mail-verification step assumed to protect acc/prod, and this branch
  grows the pool to 13×W accounts with programmatic `GLOBAL_ADMIN`.
  - **Playwright traces no longer published publicly** — one published trace held 73 `ory_kratos_session` entries. They now go to a private 14-day artifact; screenshots and the summary still publish.
  - **Fail-loud worker sizing** — an oversized `NIGHTLY_MAX_WORKERS` aborts naming the variable instead of silently halving the run and reporting green.
  - **Honest mint gate** — it had come to derive its expectation from the code path it polices; now also asserts an independent ceiling, so a duplicate mint can't hide.
  - **Skips never fail the build** — skipped/todo were recorded as failures, so ~59 phantom regressions would have appeared nightly once enforcement was enabled.
  - **Skips must cite a bug** — of 49 unconditional skips, 26 already did; the other 23 are on a closed, dated allowlist that new skips can't join and that fails when an entry goes stale.

  ## Evidence

  | Config | Environment | Wall-clock | Failures | Verdict |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Baseline (CI, W=1) | test-alkem.io | 79.2 min | 2 | — |
  | 69/39, W=5 | test-alkem.io | 56.1 min | 0 | PASS |
  | **94/14, W=5** | **test-alkem.io** | **44.5 min** | 4, all interference | **PASS** |

  `W=10` was tried and failed — setup timeouts and mass-skipped files, one taking 602 s. Resource exhaustion, not interference. **W=5 is the operating point.**

  **client-web verified**: run from this branch against the same environment, it matched the `develop` baseline exactly — 279 tests, 270 passed, 0 failed, the same 2 flaky files, 7 skipped, `exit=0`. That
  exercises the teardown rewrite across its 68 scenario-using files. Its identity path is provably unchanged (`workerCount` defaults to 1; `VITEST_POOL_ID` is never set under Playwright, so slot 0 and
  bare addresses).

  ## Known limits

  - **Notification throughput is a real ceiling.** Parallelism multiplies it roughly linearly with workers; four suites in one day backed up RabbitMQ enough to take the notifications service down.
  - **More server pods will not help** — latency measured identical at rest and under full load; the server idles while the suite runs. The remaining lever is proximity (~43–50 ms RTT from a laptop vs
  ~0.1 ms local). Traefik overhead measured ~0.1 ms.
  - Hazard rules are name/shape blocklists, not structural proofs.
  - The teardown leak summary is **per-worker**, not whole-run — a `worker_threads` consequence; CI greps the whole log.
  - The auto-invite trio's `delay(5000)`-gated assertion is a load-timing hazard: diagnosed, kept serial, not fixed.
  - Mailbox scoping is blocked — MailSlurper has no per-recipient delete, so wipe-all teardown would still race.
  - `callout-reactions.it-spec.ts` interfered once; one entry is below the demotion bar and the ledger surfaces it if it recurs.
  - The ~24 per-area developer scripts consume the changed `lib/` and are **not** covered by this feature's verification.
  - The 23 grandfathered skips are made visible, not fixed — someone still has to do that archaeology.

  - alkem-io/server#6377 — `lookup.*` fields declare `nullable` but throw `ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` (37 of 38).
  - #608 — test data not reliably cleaned up.
  - Two diagnosed, unfixed server races: the `ActorContext` cache keying, and the conversion service's empty-roleSet window. Both recorded in the spec.

- Awareness / presence
- Persistence round-trip *(opt-in)*
